subject: Copy number calling variability when the depths of normal/tumor pair differ

messages.author: 39e5c426a88af12a
messages.subject: Copy number calling variability when the depths of normal/tumor pair differ
parts:
Hi,
I tried Sequenza on 9 whole exome samples. 

Three of them did not give me accurate results with respect to copy number calls (I tried initially CNVkit to get the copy number information and used batched normal, basically pooling all the normals together, to provide a control for the analysis). 

One of the samples that dropped out was, I would say due to cellularity issue. sequenza predicted cellular content of less than 30%. I read in the paper that this might happen with samples with low cellularity. 

But the other two had really good cellularity (in the 80% range). 

From the previous reponses in this group, I read that if the depth ratio within a region fluctuate a lot, this might be an indicator of why the copy number calling is wrong. 

I checked this and attached you can see that this is indeed the case for one of the samples and not the other. 

Both samples tumor ran at a mean depth of ~40X while the normals ran at ~70X. 

Could this depth difference be the reason contributing to the wrong calls?

I do want to point out Sequenza accurately called copy number for the rest of 6 samples when compared to CNVkit and gave me more info I couldn't have received from CNVkit!

Best,
Tincy
